C.what: clinic plate WITHOUT the box: a professional treatment - the cosmetologist works on the face of the lying patient
C.prompt: Photorealistic cinematic still, 16:9, soft natural daylight. The bright treatment room of a skin-care clinic from the first reference image - pale warm-beige walls, the large white-framed window with green foliage outside, the white leather treatment couch, the potted ficus - seen from a low camera at the height of a light marble table whose polished top runs along the bottom 15 percent of the frame. The table top is empty and clean: the carton box of the reference image is not there, nothing stands on the table. Behind the table, in sharp focus: the patient lies on her back on the reclined white treatment couch, her head toward the left of the frame, her face turned up and slightly toward the camera, eyes closed, relaxed. She is the woman from the third reference image (late fifties, very short cropped platinum-blond hair under a white disposable cap, a plain white T-shirt); mature skin with fine lines, natural, not exaggerated. The cosmetologist is the woman from the second reference image (about 30, long dark wavy hair, white uniform with thin pink piping, a pendant with a blue stone on a black cord, white disposable gloves on both hands); she sits at the head of the couch, behind the patient's head, leaning over her, and with the gloved fingertips of both hands she works gently on the patient's cheeks - calm, precise, professional. The cosmetologist's face is at about 40 percent of the frame width and the patient's face at about 52 percent; between the left edge and 31 percent of the frame width there is only the empty table top and the softly lit room behind it. The right third of the frame is calm empty background. No box, no vials, no ampoules, no syringes, no bottles, no devices, no products anywhere, no captions, no text.

K3m.what: a medium close-up: the pen on P5's cheek, a needle-free syringe with a clear drop in the other hand; the whole group in the left 58 percent of the frame
images: the real pen in a gloved hand
K3m.prompt:
Photorealistic cinematic still, 16:9, soft natural daylight. The same bright treatment room, the same cosmetologist and the same patient as in the first reference image, a few minutes later, seen closer: a medium close-up of the two of them. Keep the arrangement of the first reference image: the patient is half-reclined on the white leather treatment couch, the back of her head resting on its headrest, her face turned up and slightly toward the cosmetologist, eyes closed, relaxed; the cosmetologist stands beside the couch at the left, leaning toward the patient's face.
The patient is the woman of the first reference image (late fifties, very short cropped platinum-blond hair under a white disposable cap, a plain white T-shirt; mature skin with fine lines, natural, not retouched, clean skin without make-up). The cosmetologist is the woman of the first reference image (about 30, long dark wavy hair, white uniform with thin pink piping, a pendant with a blue stone on a black cord, white disposable gloves on both hands); she looks down at the patient's cheek, calm and concentrated.
Composition: the two people are in the left part of the frame. The cosmetologist's face is at about 20 percent of the frame width, the patient's face at about 42 percent; the patient's head, her cap and the headrest end before 58 percent of the frame width. The right 42 percent of the frame is only calm softly blurred room - the pale wall and the white-framed window with green foliage outside, far out of focus; nothing else is there.
In her right hand, the one nearer to the camera, the cosmetologist holds the microneedling pen of the second reference image - exactly that device, as it looks in the gloved hand in the third reference image: the same champagne-gold body with its waist, the same faceted rose-gold ring, the same champagne front part between the ring and the short clear cartridge, the same small round button, indicator dot and flared end cap. The side of the pen with the lettering is turned away from the camera: no lettering and no text on the visible side. Do not change the device itself: the same proportions and thickness as in the photo, not thinner, not longer, not tapered, no cone, no nozzle, no cable, nothing added. She holds it like a thick pencil around the middle of its body, so that the whole pen is clearly seen from the clear cartridge to the flared end cap and her fingers do not hide the rose-gold ring. The clear cartridge end rests on the middle of the patient's cheek that faces the camera, halfway between the cheekbone and the jaw line. The third reference image shows only how this real pen looks when a gloved hand holds it against a cheek; take nothing else from it - the man of that image is not in this picture.
In her other hand she holds a slim transparent 1 ml syringe without any needle, filled with a perfectly clear colourless liquid like water, between her thumb and two fingers; its small plain plastic tip points down a few centimetres above the same cheek, close to the working end of the pen, and one clear drop hangs from the tip. Two or three tiny clear drops glisten on the skin of the cheek beside the pen's cartridge. The liquid is transparent: not golden, not white, not coloured.
The patient's eyes, nose and lips are not touched and not covered. One pen and one syringe only; nothing else in the hands. No table, no towel, no box, no bottle, no vial, no jar, no needle, no cotton pad, no second device, no blood, no redness of the skin. No text, no captions, no lettering anywhere.

Y1.what: the row of micro-channels: the still of the MITOPEN page, reused (free)

Y2m.what: the same channels, a clear solution goes down them (an edit of Y1; on MITOPEN the product is golden)
Y2m.prompt: The same illustration as in the first reference image - the same cut-away of the skin, the same row of seven thin vertical micro-channels, the same rounded cells and pink fibres, the same framing, light and empty softly blurred area on the right. Change only this: a perfectly clear, colourless solution, transparent like water, now lies as a thin glossy film on the skin surface above the channels and flows down inside every one of the seven channels as fine clear droplets with small bright highlights, filling them to their lower ends, where a soft pearly-white glow spreads gently into the surrounding tissue. The solution is transparent and colourless: not golden, not yellow, not milky, not blue. Everything else stays exactly as it is: the channels keep their place, number, width and depth. No needles, no instrument, no device, no text, no labels, no arrows, no numbers, no hands, no people.

W.from_to: K3m -> K3m (the drops and the pen at work; ends where it starts)
W.prompt: One continuous shot, no cuts; the camera stays in place with only a barely noticeable drift. The cosmetologist works with the microneedling pen on the patient's cheek: the clear drop falls from the tip of the small syringe onto the skin, and with short gentle stamping touches she moves the pen step by step along the cheek, then a few steps across it, crisscross; another clear drop falls beside the pen. The pen itself does not change its shape, colour or size; the syringe stays a slim clear syringe without a needle. The patient lies calm with her eyes closed and breathes quietly. Natural small movements, soft daylight. The shot ends in the same position as it begins. No text, no captions.

The channels keep their place, number and depth. No needles, no instruments, no text, no labels, no arrows.
